size: about 320 (300 small JSON crash reports from the generator, plus the rest)
voice: the release owner of a desktop app, writing to a developer on the team

source.licence: MPL-2.0 (Socorro); idea only (crash-report grouping), no text used

blockFields: `defects` (list of `{ "id", "signature" (the frames or message that define the group), "reports", "users" (distinct user hashes), "platforms" (object: platform to report count), "regression" (true when the defect is new in 4.2.0), "suspectChange" (a file or function from the release diff, or null), "action" (one of `hotfix`, `next-release`, `monitor`), "sampleReports" (2 to 5 report file names) }`), `excluded` (list of `{ "what", "why" }`: report groups set aside, such as other builds), `method` (one or two sentences: how the reports were grouped and counted).
kindExtra: Key shape for this task: `maxLen` on `defects` (3 to 5); for the regression defect A (the `some` matcher on `signature` matches `SyncRoot|resolve|root\.cpp`): `reports` and `users` within 10% of the planted values (use `num` bounds in the matcher), `action: hotfix`, `suspectChange` matching `root\.cpp|SyncRoot|removable|resolve`; a `none` item: no second defect whose signature matches `resolveImpl|SyncRoot` (the two inlined frames are one defect); defect B (`tray|TrayIcon`): `regression: false`; defect C (`database|sqlite|corrupt`): `users` 2 to 4; defect D (`thumbnail|OutOfMemory|OOM`): `action: hotfix`; a `none` item: no `suspectChange` matches `scheduler`; a `text` item that `excluded` or the prose names `beta` and no `sampleReports` entry is a 3.9 beta report (hand-written `hidden/reports.test.js`, add a second `tests` check); `evidence` groups: the planted hunk range in `release/4.2.0-diff.txt`, a 4.1.3 report file for B, a report whose last log lines say `dropping pending|pending uploads` for D (min 2); three `text` items for the asked facts (`9,?000|9k` near `active users|WAU|1 ?%`; `all platforms|every platform|together` near `hotfix`; `flag|kill switch|toggle|disable` in A's ticket). No exact signature string is required.

facts.answer: About 9,000 weekly active users. Use that for the 1% rule in the hotfix policy.
No. A hotfix ships on all platforms at once; we never ship one platform alone.
Yes, the removable-drive feature has a server-side flag. We can turn it off for everyone within an hour.

brief: Phase: issue triage (crash reports after a release). Role: developer (release owner). Folder: `crashes/` with about 300 JSON crash reports (id, timestamp, app version, OS and version, user hash, top 8 stack frames, last 5 log lines) written by the generator; `release/4.2.0-diff.txt`, a unified diff of 4.2.0 against 4.1.3 over about 12 files, one hunk in `src/sync/root.cpp` introducing the top defect (a null path when the sync folder is on a removable drive that is unplugged) and a decoy hunk in `src/sync/scheduler.cpp` changing retry timing that shows up in many last-log lines ('retry scheduled') but in no crashing frame; `release/notes-4.2.0.md` mentioning the removable-drive feature; `release/history.md` (4.1.3 three weeks ago, 4.2.0 Monday); `docs/hotfix-policy.md` (hotfix when a defect hits more than 1% of weekly active users or causes any data loss; otherwise next release; it does not say the WAU number); `docs/crash-collector.md` (field meanings; the Windows build inlines small functions, so one crash may show two top frames). Plant: defect A, the regression, about 170 reports and 120 users on Windows and macOS, two Windows top-frame variants (`SyncRoot::resolve`, `SyncRoot::resolveImpl`) that are one defect; defect B, about 60 reports and 55 users, macOS, tray icon code, also present in about 15 reports from 4.1.3 users, so not a regression; defect C, about 40 reports but 3 users (one user crashes every 5 minutes), a corrupt local database; defect D, about 20 reports and 20 users, Linux, out of memory in the thumbnail cache, last log lines say 'dropping pending uploads' (data loss); about 10 noise reports from build 3.9.0-beta2. The request asks how many distinct defects there are, how big each is in reports and users, which change in the diff most likely caused the biggest, which need a hotfix before Friday, one ticket per defect, the document at the given path ending with the JSON block, and evidence cited as `path:line`. The request must not name the inlining, the policy thresholds, the decoy or the beta build. The lazy answer makes one defect per top frame, all next-release, no suspect; the copy answer pastes a histogram of top frames; both must fail. The three scripted facts (weekly active users, whether a hotfix may ship one platform, whether the feature has a flag) are not in the folder; the reference asks for them and uses them (the 1% rule needs the WAU; the flag is A's mitigation).
